title: Payroll Tax Withholding Calculation
problem: Accountants manually calculate federal income tax withholding, FICA, Medicare, and state taxes for every payroll cycle. Errors lead to IRS penalties under Section 6656 (up to 15% of underpayment) and employee complaints. During peak periods with 50-80 hour weeks, calculation mistakes multiply.
who: Staff and senior accountants handling payroll for small to mid-size businesses

skill_spec.name: Payroll Tax Withholding Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates net pay including federal income tax, FICA, Medicare, and state withholdings from gross salary
skill_spec.formula_hint: Taxable income = gross - pre_tax_deductions. Federal tax from 2026 brackets. Social Security = 6.2% up to wage base ($176,100 for 2026). Medicare = 1.45% + 0.9% additional over $200k. State tax by state brackets.

example_queries: Calculate net pay for an employee earning $85,000 annually, paid biweekly, single filer in California
How much federal and state tax should I withhold from a $4,200 biweekly paycheck for a married employee in Texas?
What's the total employer payroll tax cost for a $120,000 salary?

title: IRS Penalty and Interest Estimation
problem: When clients file late or underpay taxes, accountants must manually calculate penalties and interest using complex IRS rules (failure-to-file, failure-to-pay, accuracy-related penalties). Getting these wrong means either overpaying or getting a surprise IRS notice. Penalty calculations compound daily and reference fluctuating federal rates.
who: Tax accountants and CPAs handling individual and business returns

skill_spec.name: IRS Penalty & Interest Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Estimates IRS penalties and accrued interest for late filing, late payment, and underpayment of estimated taxes

outputs.name: total_due
outputs.label: Total amount due including penalty and interest

skill_spec.formula_hint: Failure-to-file: 5% per month up to 25%. Failure-to-pay: 0.5% per month up to 25%. Interest: federal short-term rate + 3%, compounded daily. Accuracy-related: 20% of underpayment under Section 6662.

example_queries: My client owes $15,000 on their 1040 and filed 3 months late. What's the total penalty and interest?
Estimate the failure-to-pay penalty for a $50,000 corporate tax balance due April 15 if paid September 30
What's the accuracy-related penalty on a $30,000 understatement?

title: Depreciation Schedule Calculation
problem: Accountants spend hours building and maintaining depreciation schedules for client assets using MACRS, Section 179, and bonus depreciation rules. The 2026 phase-down of bonus depreciation (now 40%) and varying recovery periods by asset class make this error-prone. Mistakes directly impact taxable income and financial statements.
who: Tax and corporate accountants managing fixed assets for businesses

skill_spec.name: MACRS Depreciation Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates depreciation expense using MACRS, Section 179 deduction, and bonus depreciation with full multi-year schedule
skill_spec.formula_hint: MACRS percentages by class (e.g., 7-year: 14.29/24.49/17.49/12.49/8.93/8.92/8.93/4.46). Bonus depreciation 40% for 2026. Section 179 limit ~$1.25M for 2026. Apply Section 179 first, then bonus, then MACRS on remainder.

example_queries: Calculate MACRS depreciation for a $250,000 piece of equipment placed in service in March 2026, 7-year property
What's the first-year deduction if I take Section 179 plus bonus depreciation on a $500,000 asset?
Generate a full depreciation schedule for a $1.2M commercial building placed in service this year

title: Tax Filing Deadline Calendar
problem: Accountants juggle dozens of federal and state filing deadlines across multiple entity types (individuals, S-Corps, C-Corps, partnerships, nonprofits, payroll). Missing a single deadline triggers automatic penalties. With 50-80 hour weeks during tax season, tracking all deadlines across clients is a constant source of anxiety - it's the #1 fear reported by professionals.
who: All tax accountants and CPAs, especially those managing multiple clients

skill_spec.name: Tax Filing Deadline Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Instant lookup of all federal and state tax filing deadlines, extension dates, and estimated payment due dates by entity type
skill_spec.data_domain: Federal and state tax filing deadlines for all entity types in 2026

example_queries: When is the filing deadline for a partnership return in 2026?
What are all the estimated tax payment due dates for 2026?
My S-Corp client has a fiscal year ending June 30 - when is the return due?

title: Year-End Financial Close Checklist
problem: Year-end close involves 30+ steps across multiple accounts, departments, and systems. Missing a step (unrecorded accruals, unreconciled accounts, missed cutoff adjustments) leads to material misstatements, restatements, and potential SOX violations for public companies. The December-January crunch leaves little room for error.
who: Corporate accountants and controllers managing year-end close

skill_spec.name: Year-End Financial Close Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Comprehensive step-by-step checklist for year-end close covering all accounts, reconciliations, adjustments, and compliance requirements
steps: Step 1: Verify all sub-ledgers are posted to the general ledger
Step 2: Complete bank reconciliations for all accounts
Step 3: Reconcile intercompany accounts and eliminate intercompany transactions
Step 4: Review and adjust accrued expenses (wages, interest, utilities, taxes)
Step 5: Verify revenue recognition cutoff - ensure proper period assignment
Step 6: Calculate and record depreciation and amortization for the period
Step 7: Perform inventory count and adjust for obsolescence/write-downs
Step 8: Reconcile accounts receivable and assess allowance for doubtful accounts
Step 9: Reconcile accounts payable and search for unrecorded liabilities (SURL)
Step 10: Review and adjust prepaid expenses and deferred revenue
Step 11: Calculate and record income tax provision (ASC 740)
Step 12: Prepare trial balance and review for unusual balances
Step 13: Record all adjusting journal entries with proper documentation
Step 14: Prepare financial statements (BS, P&L, Cash Flow, Equity)
Step 15: Perform flux analysis - compare to prior year and budget
Step 16: Prepare footnote disclosures and management discussion
Step 17: Obtain management review and sign-off
Step 18: Archive workpapers and supporting documentation
warnings: Warning: SOX Section 302/404 requires CEO/CFO certification of internal controls - ensure all control testing is documented
Warning: Revenue recognition must comply with ASC 606 - review contract modifications
Warning: Lease accounting under ASC 842 - verify all leases are properly recorded

example_queries: Give me a complete year-end close checklist for a mid-size company
What steps should I follow for year-end close at a public company with SOX requirements?
What are the most commonly missed items in year-end financial close?

title: Engagement Letter Generator
problem: CPAs must issue engagement letters for every new client and service - audit, review, compilation, tax preparation. Each letter requires specific AICPA-compliant language, scope definitions, fee structures, and limitation of liability clauses. Writing these from scratch or adapting old templates is time-consuming and risks omitting required provisions.
who: CPAs and firm managers onboarding new clients or changing engagement scope

skill_spec.name: CPA Engagement Letter Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates AICPA-compliant engagement letters for audit, review, compilation, and tax preparation services
skill_spec.structure_hint: Letterhead -> Date -> Client address -> Engagement objective and scope -> Management responsibilities -> Auditor/CPA responsibilities -> Deliverables -> Fee and billing terms -> Limitation of liability -> Dispute resolution -> Signature blocks. Must reference applicable AICPA standards (AU-C 210 for audits, AR-C 80/90 for compilations/reviews).

example_queries: Generate an audit engagement letter for ABC Corporation, fiscal year ending December 31, 2026, fixed fee of $45,000
Create a tax preparation engagement letter for an individual client
Draft a compilation engagement letter for a small partnership

title: Audit Procedures and Substantive Testing Checklist
problem: Auditors must design and execute substantive procedures for every significant account balance and transaction class. Missing a key procedure or failing to document it properly leads to PCAOB inspection deficiencies. With 39 enforcement actions in 2025 and continuing PCAOB scrutiny, incomplete audit documentation is a career-threatening risk.
who: External auditors at all levels, especially seniors planning audit fieldwork

skill_spec.name: Audit Substantive Testing Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates a tailored checklist of substantive audit procedures by account area with PCAOB/AICPA compliance requirements
steps: Step 1: Obtain understanding of the entity and its environment (AS 2110)
Step 2: Assess risk of material misstatement for each significant account
Step 3: Design substantive procedures responsive to identified risks
Step 4: Cash - confirm bank balances, test reconciling items, perform cutoff testing
Step 5: Receivables - confirm balances, test aging, evaluate allowance estimate
Step 6: Inventory - observe physical count, test pricing, evaluate obsolescence
Step 7: Fixed assets - vouch additions/disposals, recalculate depreciation, test for impairment
Step 8: Payables - search for unrecorded liabilities (SURL), confirm significant balances
Step 9: Revenue - test transactions near period end for cutoff, agree to contracts (ASC 606)
Step 10: Expenses - perform analytical procedures, vouch unusual items
Step 11: Evaluate audit evidence sufficiency and appropriateness
Step 12: Document conclusions for each significant account in workpapers
warnings: Warning: PCAOB AS 1215 requires documentation sufficient for an experienced auditor to understand the work performed
Warning: All confirmations must be controlled by the auditor per AS 2310
Warning: Fraud risk procedures required per AS 2401 - test journal entries and estimates

example_queries: What substantive procedures should I perform for accounts receivable in an audit?
Give me a complete audit testing checklist for a manufacturing company
What are the PCAOB documentation requirements for substantive testing?

title: Estimated Tax Payment Calculator
problem: Accountants calculate quarterly estimated tax payments for clients to avoid underpayment penalties under IRC 6654 (individuals) and 6655 (corporations). The safe harbor rules (100% or 110% of prior year tax), annualized income method, and varying state requirements make this calculation complex. Getting it wrong means penalties or clients overpaying and losing cash flow.
who: Tax accountants managing quarterly estimated payments for self-employed and business clients

skill_spec.name: Estimated Tax Payment Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates required quarterly estimated tax payments using safe harbor rules to avoid IRS underpayment penalties

inputs.name: withholding_credits
inputs.label: Expected withholding and credits for current year (USD)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Individual safe harbor: lesser of 90% current year tax or 100% prior year (110% if AGI > $150k). Corporate: lesser of 100% current year or 100% prior year. Quarterly = annual required / 4. Subtract withholding. Penalty under IRC 6654 uses federal short-term rate + 3%.

example_queries: My client had $50,000 tax liability last year and AGI of $200,000. What should their quarterly estimated payments be?
Calculate safe harbor estimated payments for a corporation with $300,000 prior year tax
Will my client owe an underpayment penalty if they paid $10,000 per quarter but owe $55,000 total?

title: Bank Reconciliation Discrepancy Advisor
problem: Bank reconciliations are performed daily or weekly, and discrepancies are inevitable - outstanding checks, deposits in transit, bank errors, unauthorized transactions, timing differences. Identifying the cause and correct adjustment requires experience. Junior staff waste hours investigating routine variances, while missed discrepancies can signal fraud or errors.
who: Staff accountants and bookkeepers performing regular bank reconciliations

skill_spec.name: Bank Reconciliation Troubleshooter
skill_spec.one_liner: Diagnoses common bank reconciliation discrepancies and recommends the correct adjusting entries
skill_spec.expertise_area: Bank reconciliation discrepancy analysis and resolution

example_queries: My bank reconciliation is off by $1,247.50 - the bank balance is higher than the book balance. What should I check?
I have an outstanding check from 6 months ago that still hasn't cleared. What should I do?
How do I handle a bank error on the reconciliation?

problem: When a client receives an IRS audit notice, accountants must quickly determine the audit type (correspondence, office, field), assess the risk, gather documentation, and respond within tight deadlines. Fear of audit deficiencies is a top professional concern. Wrong responses can escalate issues, trigger broader examinations, or waive client rights.
who: Tax CPAs and Enrolled Agents representing clients before the IRS

skill_spec.name: IRS Audit Response Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Guides CPAs through IRS audit response strategy including documentation requirements, taxpayer rights, and resolution options
skill_spec.expertise_area: IRS examination response and taxpayer representation

example_queries: My client got a CP2000 notice for unreported 1099 income of $25,000. What's the best response strategy?
How should I prepare for an IRS field audit of a small business?
The IRS is proposing to disallow $40,000 in business deductions. Should we agree, protest, or go to Appeals?

title: Management Representation Letter Generator
problem: At the conclusion of every audit, management must provide a representation letter confirming key assertions. Auditors must ensure the letter covers all required representations per AU-C 580 / AS 2805 and includes engagement-specific items. Omitting required representations is an audit deficiency frequently cited in PCAOB inspections.
who: Audit seniors and managers preparing for audit completion

skill_spec.name: Management Representation Letter Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates AU-C 580 / PCAOB AS 2805 compliant management representation letters tailored to the specific audit engagement

variables.name: special_matters
variables.label: Special matters to address (litigation, related parties, subsequent events, going concern)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Date -> Addressed to auditor -> Opening paragraph identifying financial statements -> Standard representations (completeness, GAAP compliance, estimates, fraud, subsequent events, related parties, litigation, going concern) -> Engagement-specific representations -> CEO/CFO signatures. Reference AU-C 580 for nonissuers, AS 2805 for issuers.

example_queries: Generate a management representation letter for a public company audit, fiscal year ending December 31, 2026
What representations must be included in a management letter for a company with pending litigation?
Create a rep letter for a nonprofit audit under AU-C 580

title: SOX Compliance Internal Controls Reference
problem: Public company auditors must evaluate internal controls over financial reporting per SOX Section 404. Identifying which controls are key, understanding control objectives for each assertion, and mapping controls to COSO framework components requires constant reference to standards. Misclassifying a control deficiency (deficiency vs. significant deficiency vs. material weakness) has major consequences.
who: External and internal auditors at public companies

skill_spec.name: SOX Internal Controls Reference Guide
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick reference for SOX 404 compliance including COSO framework mapping, control classifications, deficiency evaluation criteria, and PCAOB inspection focus areas
skill_spec.data_domain: Sarbanes-Oxley Section 404 internal control requirements and PCAOB auditing standards

data_hints.source_law: Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, PCAOB Auditing Standards

deficiency_levels.deficiency: Control does not allow timely prevention/detection but likelihood of misstatement is remote
deficiency_levels.significant_deficiency: Less severe than material weakness but important enough to merit attention
deficiency_levels.material_weakness: Reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be prevented or detected

example_queries: What's the difference between a significant deficiency and a material weakness under SOX?
What are the five COSO components and what controls map to each?
What are the PCAOB's most common SOX 404 inspection findings in 2025-2026?

title: Lease Accounting Calculator (ASC 842)
problem: ASC 842 requires lessees to recognize right-of-use assets and lease liabilities on the balance sheet. Accountants must calculate present value of lease payments, determine lease classification (operating vs finance), and generate amortization schedules. The calculations involve discount rates, variable payments, and modification accounting that are tedious and error-prone in spreadsheets.
who: Corporate accountants and auditors dealing with lease accounting

skill_spec.name: ASC 842 Lease Accounting Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates right-of-use asset, lease liability, and generates full amortization schedule under ASC 842
skill_spec.formula_hint: Lease liability = PV of lease payments at discount rate. ROU asset = lease liability + initial direct costs + prepaid rent - lease incentives. Operating: straight-line expense. Finance: amortization of ROU asset + interest on liability. Interest = beginning liability * monthly rate.

example_queries: Calculate the ROU asset and lease liability for a 5-year office lease at $8,000/month with a 5% discount rate
Generate an ASC 842 amortization schedule for a finance lease of $120,000 over 48 months
What journal entries do I record at lease commencement for an operating lease?
